quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes driving conditions less than perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes driving conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when any condition is not perfect. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are at the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your recovery from headlight glare, and increases risky behavior.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Only stop signs are shaped like octagons. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop completely before going forward.

questions.question: What should you do when the driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Slow down to give them space in front of your car to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them space in front of your car to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when someone wants to pass you. This gives them enough room to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no train visible or heard, you must stop if:
questions.correctAnswerText: Any of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights flash, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible. If you are unsure if it is safe to cross, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, pull over to the curb or road edge immediately and stop.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, drivers of small vehicles must be ready for:

options.text: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through if no traffic is crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mark dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts you?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of these.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating before or while you drink slows alcohol absorption slightly, but it cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other cars and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: When another car is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move to it. If no right lane is open, wait until ahead is clear, then slow down gradually. This lets the tailgater pass. Never stop suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Look for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers. Look for other drivers who might be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: You are on a divided highway with multiple lanes and see or hear an emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move your car to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move your car to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down, clear the path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: On long trips, you can avoid getting sleepy by:

options.text: Moving your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking breaks to rest regularly.
questions.explanation: To avoid drowsiness on long trips, take regular breaks. Rest and stretch your body, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A one-way sign shows the direction traffic must travel.

questions.question: Defensive driving means:

options.text: Spotting dangerous driving situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Blocking bad drivers by staying ahead of them.
Following the car in front of you very closely.
Quickly switching lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous driving situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means noticing dangerous situations and taking action before an accident happens. It helps protect you from reckless, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, you should:

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to the one you came from.
Turn into the lane with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to the one you came from.
questions.explanation: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, turn into the lane nearest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic light ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: You are entering a reduced speed zone.
You are leaving a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are leaving a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: Do not go faster than the school zone speed limit when it is in effect. The "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: The best safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags used with seat belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Drive only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe distance lets you react to problems without emergency stops. Emergency stops can cause the car behind you to hit your vehicle.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see:
questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection, the light turns yellow. Your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: Yellow means the light will turn red soon. Be prepared to stop safely before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: Is a distraction.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by taking your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers making a left turn at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Always use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs indicate:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you of railroad crossings. Yield to trains and do not try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.
questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a crash.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic already on the freeway, and match the speed of that traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic already on the freeway, and match the speed of that traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.
